name: STM32C031C6T6
title: Arm Cortex-M0+ 48 MHz microcontroller, 16 or 32 KB flash, 12 KB SRAM, 2.0 V to 3.6 V
summary: An entry-level Cortex-M0+ microcontroller family at up to 48 MHz on one 2.0 V to 3.6 V supply, with 16 or 32 Kbytes of flash and 12 Kbytes of parity-checked SRAM. It has a 12-bit 2.5 MSps ADC with up to 19 external inputs, an advanced-control timer and four general-purpose 16-bit timers, two USARTs, an SPI that doubles as I2S, an I2C with Fast-mode Plus, a calendar RTC, three DMA channels and a 48 MHz RC oscillator trimmed to ±1 %. Packages run from TSSOP20 to LQFP48 and UFQFPN48. STM32C031C6T6 is the 32 Kbyte LQFP48 part with 45 I/Os for -40 °C to 85 °C ambient.
key_figures: Arm Cortex-M0+ with MPU, up to 48 MHz
16 or 32 Kbytes flash, 12 Kbytes SRAM with parity
2.0 V to 3.6 V, single VDD/VDDA pin
3.05 mA typ at 48 MHz from flash (HSE bypass, 3 V, 25 °C)

circuits.title: Power supply scheme
circuits.description: The single VDD/VDDA pin takes the 2.0 V to 3.6 V rail and feeds the regulator, the I/O ring and the ADC; a 100 nF and a 4.7 µF ceramic capacitor tie it to VSS/VSSA, mounted at or under the pin pair. On 48-pin parts VREF+ takes the ADC reference with its own 100 nF to ground.
notes: Packages without a VREF+ pin have VREF+ joined to VDD/VDDA inside.

circuits.title: 8 MHz crystal on the HSE oscillator
circuits.description: An 8 MHz crystal or ceramic resonator sits between OSC_IN and OSC_OUT, with a load capacitor from each end to ground; the 200 kΩ feedback resistor RF is on the chip. A series resistor REXT between the crystal and OSC_OUT is sized to the crystal. CL1 and CL2 are normally equal, 5 pF to 20 pF high-frequency ceramics; the crystal's rated load is their series value plus about 10 pF of pin and board capacitance.
notes: A resonator with built-in capacitors takes the place of Y1, C1 and C2.
The crystal and its capacitors go as close to the oscillator pins as possible.

circuits.title: 32.768 kHz crystal on the LSE oscillator
circuits.description: A 32.768 kHz crystal between OSCX_IN and OSCX_OUT with a load capacitor from each pin to ground clocks the RTC. The amplifier's drive is chosen in software with LSEDRV. No resistor is fitted across the crystal: none is needed and one is not allowed.
notes: A resonator with built-in capacitors takes the place of Y1, C1 and C2.
The crystal and its capacitors go as close to the oscillator pins as possible.

circuits.title: NRST pin protection
circuits.description: A 0.1 µF capacitor from NRST to ground, placed close to the chip, keeps stray pulses from resetting it, and a push-button to ground gives a manual reset. The pull-up RPU is inside. Whatever drives NRST has to take it below VIL(NRST) max, or the reset is missed.

circuits.title: ADC input connection
circuits.description: A source VAIN reaches an analog input through its own resistance RAIN, while the pad and the board add Cparasitic to ground. RAIN stays at or under 50 kΩ and under the limit for the chosen resolution and sampling time. A large Cparasitic costs accuracy, which a slower ADC clock wins back.
notes: PA0 (ADC_IN0) stands for any ADC_INx pin.

operation.text: Arm Cortex-M0+ with a two-stage pipeline, single-cycle multiplier and a memory protection unit, running at up to 48 MHz. The MPU guards memory regions between tasks, typically under an RTOS, and can be left unused.

16 or 32 Kbytes of flash for code and data. Option bytes set readout protection in three levels: level 0 none; level 1 blocks flash reads and writes whenever debug is attached or the part boots from RAM or the bootloader; level 2 switches off the serial-wire debug, RAM boot and bootloader selection for good and cannot be undone. Write protection covers two areas per bank, in 2 Kbyte steps, against erase and programming.
12 Kbytes of SRAM with hardware parity, read and written at CPU speed with no wait states. A parity error can trigger a break on TIM1, TIM16 and TIM17.

At start-up the BOOT0 pin (shared with PA14) and the boot-selector option bit choose user flash, system memory or embedded SRAM. The bootloader in system memory reprograms the flash over USART on PA9/PA10 or over I2C on PB6/PB7.
A CRC unit with programmable polynomial and size computes signatures, for example to check flash integrity at run time against a reference stored at link time, as used for IEC 60335-1.

One VDD/VDDA pin powers everything: the regulator and system analog (VDD), the ADC (VDDA) and the I/O ring (VDDIO1), all at the same 2.0 V to 3.6 V. Operation starts once VDD passes VPOR max (2.0 V) and is held down to VPDR min (1.96 V). VREF+ lies between 2 V and VDDA and may be grounded when no analog peripheral uses it; packages without the pin join it to VDD inside. An internal linear regulator makes VCORE for the logic, SRAM and flash; the flash also draws on VDD.

The VDD/VDDA and VSS/VSSA pair takes 100 nF plus 4.7 µF of ceramic capacitance, placed as close to the pins as possible or beneath them on the far side of the board. VREF+ takes 100 nF. The 100 nF part should be a good-quality ceramic close to the chip.

A POR/PDR circuit, active in every mode but Shutdown, holds the part in reset below its threshold with no external reset circuit. The brownout reset is turned on and set in the option bytes, choosing one of four rising and four falling thresholds. POR release adds a 270 µs typical delay after VDD crosses VPOR.
The regulator feeds most digital circuits. In Standby and Shutdown it is turned off and its output floats, so it draws almost nothing.

Run follows any reset. Sleep stops only the CPU; any peripheral interrupt or event wakes it. Stop halts every VCORE clock, HSE and HSI48 included, but keeps SRAM and registers; LSE and LSI may keep running with the RTC, a peripheral that needs HSI48 can restart it, and on exit HSI48 starts and HSISYS becomes the system clock. Standby turns the regulator off and loses register contents except the 16-bit backup registers; POR/PDR stays active, each I/O can keep a pull-up, pull-down or none, and the part wakes on NRST, IWDG reset, a WKUP pin edge (rising or falling, selectable) or an LSE failure. Shutdown is the lowest state: regulator, HSI48, LSI and HSE all off, no RTC, no BOR or any supply monitoring, SRAM and registers lost; only NRST or a WKUP pin edge wakes it.

During reset and as it ends, the I/O Schmitt triggers are off to save current. On an internally caused reset the NRST pull-up is turned off. NRST has a permanent 25 kΩ to 55 kΩ pull-up and a filter that ignores pulses up to 70 ns and passes those of 350 ns or more.

System clock sources: HSE with a 4 MHz to 48 MHz crystal or ceramic resonator, or an external clock in bypass; HSI48, a 48 MHz internal RC trimmable in software (±1 %); LSE, a 32.768 kHz crystal oscillator with four drive levels or bypass; LSI, a 32 kHz RC (±5 %) that also clocks the IWDG. The RTC can run from LSE, LSI or HSE/32. I2S, the USARTs, I2C and the ADC can take their own kernel clocks. The clock security system switches to HSI48 or LSI if HSE or LSE fails, with an optional interrupt. MCO puts an internal clock on a pin; LSCO puts out LSI or LSE in every low-power mode. AHB and APB run at up to 48 MHz through prescalers.

CL1 and CL2 for the HSE crystal are high-quality high-frequency ceramics, usually 5 pF to 20 pF and equal, chosen so their series value plus about 10 pF of pin and board capacitance matches the crystal's rated load. Crystal and capacitors sit as close to the oscillator pins as possible to limit distortion and start-up time. ST application note AN2867 covers crystal choice. The LSE needs no resistor across the crystal and one must not be fitted.

Every GPIO can be a push-pull or open-drain output, an input (floating, pulled up or pulled down), or an alternate function; most also carry analog or special digital functions. The alternate-function setup can be locked against stray writes. Up to 45 I/Os, all usable as external interrupt lines; inputs meet both CMOS and TTL levels without configuration. Each pin sinks or sources up to ±6 mA, or ±15 mA with relaxed output levels, within the 20 mA per pin and 80 mA total ratings and the 100 mA supply-pin limits.

A floating input can sit at a middle level or toggle from noise and draw Schmitt-trigger current. Unused pins go to analog mode, or are held at a fixed level with the internal pull resistor or as an output. ADC inputs are set to analog mode. An input with pull-up held low draws current through the pull-up.
SYSCFG_CFGR1 moves PA9 and PA10 onto the pins normally carrying PA11 and PA12.

A three-channel DMA controller moves data between memory and peripherals in any direction, with four software priority levels per channel, independent source and destination widths, circular buffers and up to 2^16 - 1 items per transfer; each channel raises half-transfer, complete and error interrupts. DMAMUX routes any request line to any channel, optionally synchronised to events, and can generate requests itself.

The NVIC handles 32 maskable lines, the NMI and 10 core exceptions with 4 priority levels, tail-chaining and hardware vector fetch. The EXTI detects rising, falling or both edges on GPIO and some peripheral lines, catches pulses shorter than a clock period, and latches events in Stop mode so the wake-up source can be read.

A 12-bit successive-approximation ADC with up to 19 external and 2 internal channels (temperature sensor, VREFINT), single or scan conversion, up to 2.5 MSps independent of the CPU clock. It powers down between conversions, works over the whole VDD range, has an analog watchdog on one, some or all channels and can be triggered by the timers and served by DMA. A calibration after every power-up is recommended. The source impedance limit depends on resolution and sampling time, up to 50 kΩ at 160.5 cycles.

The temperature sensor output rises linearly with temperature, about 2.53 mV/°C, and is read through the ADC; its offset varies from part to part, so for absolute readings each part carries a factory value TS_CAL1 taken at 30 °C. VREFINT, a bandgap near 1.212 V, is also measured per part at 30 °C and 3.0 V and stored.

TIM1 is an advanced-control timer: four channels, three complementary outputs with dead-time insertion, edge or centre-aligned PWM, one-pulse mode, and break inputs; in debug its outputs can be turned off with the counter frozen. TIM3 has four channels with up/down counting, encoder support and DMA. TIM14 has one channel. TIM16 and TIM17 each have one channel with a complementary output and DMA. All are 16-bit at up to 48 MHz and can be chained through the timer link.

The IWDG has an 8-bit prescaler and a 12-bit down-counter with a refresh window, runs from the LSI, keeps running in Stop and Standby, and is turned on by hardware or software through the option bytes. The WWDG is a 7-bit down-counter on the system clock with an early-warning interrupt. SysTick is a 24-bit down-counter for an RTOS tick or general timing.

A BCD calendar RTC with sub-seconds, alarm, timestamp pin, 50/60 Hz reference-clock input, smooth calibration in 0.95 ppm steps and shift correction of 1 to 32767 clock pulses. It sits in the RTC domain, is supplied from VCORE, runs in Run, Sleep and Stop, and its alarm or timestamp can wake the part. The RTC is off in Standby and Shutdown.

One I2C interface for Standard (100 kbit/s), Fast (400 kbit/s) and Fast-mode Plus (1 Mbit/s with high-drive I/O), master or slave, 7- or 10-bit addressing, clock stretching, SMBus 3.0 with PEC, ARP and alert, PMBus 1.3, analog and digital noise filters, an independent kernel clock and wake-up from Stop on address match. The SDA and SCL pins are not true open-drain: the PMOS to VDDIO1 is off in open-drain mode but still present. The analog filter's suppression limit lies between 50 ns and 260 ns.

Two USARTs at up to 6 Mbit/s with CTS/RTS and RS485 driver enable, multiprocessor mode, synchronous master mode and single-wire half-duplex. USART1 adds smartcard, IrDA, LIN, Modbus, auto baud rate, receiver timeout and a separate clock domain that wakes the part from Stop on a start bit, any frame or a chosen frame. Both work with DMA.

One SPI at up to 24 Mbit/s, master or slave, full-duplex, half-duplex or simplex, 4- to 16-bit frames, NSS pulse mode, TI mode, hardware CRC and DMA. In I2S mode it handles four audio standards, master or slave, 16/24/32-bit data at 8 kHz to 192 kHz sampling, and as master can output a 256 × Fs clock.
Serial wire debug through SWDIO (PA13) and SWCLK (PA14), which come out of reset in that role with a pull-up on PA13 and a pull-down on PA14.

Voltages are referred to VSS. Minimum and maximum figures hold over the worst case of temperature, supply and frequency, production-tested at 25 °C and TA max; those from characterization are mean ±3σ. Typical figures are at 25 °C and VDD = VDDA = 3 V and are untested guidance; typical ADC accuracy covers 95 % of parts (mean ±2σ). Pin parameters are measured with 50 pF on the pin.
Supply currents are taken with every I/O in analog mode, peripherals off unless named, the fewest flash wait states for the clock, and fPCLK = fHCLK. The current is measured into the VDD/VDDA pin.

Susceptibility is tested by ESD on the pins (IEC 61000-4-2) and fast bursts on VDD and VSS through 100 pF (IEC 61000-4-4) while the part toggles two LEDs; a reset restores operation. Firmware should cope with a corrupted program counter, unexpected resets and corrupted critical data. Forcing NRST or the oscillator pins low for one second reproduces most common failures as a pre-qualification check (ST application note AN1015).
TA max applies at full dissipation; with less dissipation the ambient may rise further so long as TJ stays within its limit (105 °C, 125 °C or 130 °C by temperature suffix).
